newsitem.title: USA: Ply Gem to merge with Atrium for $482 mln.
newsitem.headline: Ply Gem to merge with Atrium for $482 mln.

text.p: Ply Gem Industries Inc said Wednesday it has entered a definitive agreement to be purchased by privately owned Atrium Corp in a $482 million transaction.
The company said in addition to paying $18.75 per share in cash for Ply Gem stock, Atrium must also assume Ply Gem's debt. The deal is expected to close in the third quarter.
Atrium is controlled by the investment firm Hicks, Muse, Tate and Furst Inc, which has pledged $140 million of equity capital to finance the merger.
Ply Gem has long-term debt totaling about $113 million, according to Standard & Poors.
Ply Gem is a producer of building and home improvement products used primarily in the remodeling and construction of residential properties.
The combined companies will have annual sales of about $1 billion, according to a press release from Hicks, Muse said.

"We acquired Atrium this past November with the intent of pursuing a buy-and-build strategy to strengthen and diversify the company," said Atrium chairman and Hicks, Muse chief operating officer John Muse. "The Ply Gem merger achieves our objective of creating a market leader which is national in scope and has a diversified product line and customer base."
The two companies were not immediately available for comment.
